routes.label: Find all points at the two heights

question: A particle is placed on the parabola \(y=x^2-x-6\) at a point \(P\) whose ordinate is \(6.\) It is allowed to roll along the parabola until it reaches the nearest point \(Q\) whose ordinate is \(-6.\) The horizontal distance traveled by the particle (the numerical value of the difference in the abscissas of \(P\) and \(Q\)) is:
solution:
The requested distance depends on the abscissas, or \(x\)-coordinates, so first find every point at each stated ordinate, or \(y\)-coordinate.

At \(P\), the ordinate is \(6\), so
\[
x^2-x-6=6
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(x-4)(x+3)=0.
\]
Thus \(P\) is either \((4,6)\) or \((-3,6)\). At a possible destination \(Q\),
\[
x^2-x-6=-6
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
x(x-1)=0.
\]
The only destinations are therefore \((0,-6)\) and \((1,-6)\).

Both destinations lie \(12\) units below \(P\). By the Pythagorean theorem, the one with smaller horizontal separation is nearer. If \(P=(4,6)\), the horizontal separations are \(4\) and \(3\), so \(Q=(1,-6)\). If \(P=(-3,6)\), they are \(3\) and \(4\), so \(Q=(0,-6)\). These nearer destinations are also the first points of ordinate \(-6\) encountered along the parabola from their respective starting points.

In either case, the horizontal distance is \(3\), choice C.
